full_judgment:
MR. ABDUS SALAM MAMUN, J:  This Jail appeal has been directed against the impugned judgment and order dated 20.3.2004 passed by the Sessions Judge, Mymensingh, in Sessions Case No. 120 of 2003arising out of Tarakanda Police Station Case No.8 dated 18.6.2002 corresponding to G. R. No. 294(2)02 under Section 302/34 of the Penal Code convicting the accused-appellant Shahabuddin (convict- prisoner) under Section 302 of the Penal Code and sentencing him to suffer imprisonment for life and also to pay fine of Tk.2,000/- in default to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 6(six) months more. 

 3. On receipt of the said FIR the Tarakanda Police started the aforesaid P.S case which was investigated into by the Officer-in-charge of the Tarakanda Police Station, who during investigation, visited the place of occurrence, prepared the sketch map with separate index, seized alamats recorded the statements of the witnesses under Section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, collected the post-mortem report and on finding a good prima facie case submitted a charge sheet against the accused-appellant along with his parents and one Md. Harun praying for their trial. 

 4. The case was ultimately received by the learned Sessions Judge, Mymensingh for trial  who framed charges against all the accused persons including the present appellant under Section 302/34 of the Penal Code and while the same was read over to them they all pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. 

 5. During the trial of the Case, the prosecution produced as many as 12 witnesses, of which PW1 Md. Waliullah is the informant, PW2 Shamim is the son of the accused Shahabuddin and the deceased, PW3 Sharmin is their daughter, PW4 Jobeda Khatoon is the mother of the deceased and mother-in-law of the accused Shahabuddin, PW6 A. Aziz is his neighbour and PW 8 and 10 are the police personnels. PW11 Saima Saheen Sultan is a Magistrate and PW12 Doctor Abul Monsur is the doctor who held the Post-Mortem examination of the deceased. 

 11. PW8 Mahbub Alam is the police officer who made the inquest report, Ext.3 and PW1 0 Sheikh Abul -Mannan is the Investigation Officer of the Case. 

 The learned Advocate has argued that the learned trial Judge was under obligation to bring all the incriminating materials to the notice of the accused-appellant at the time of his examination under Section 342 Cr.P.C so to enable him to offer a proper reply and make appropriate defence, which in the instant case, the learned trial Judge has failed to do. All the incriminating .materials, i-e, specific evidence of the individual witnesses have not been placed before the accused-appellant during his examination under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and as such it is a violation of the- mandatory provisions of law which has vitiated the trial. 

 From the above statements, it is clear that he was fully aware that he was facing the charge of killing of' his wife to which he offered an explanation that his wife was caught by diarrhea in the house of his mother-in-law. He had the clear understanding that the death of his wife was the fact in issue in his Case and he took the plea that he did not know how his wife died. 

 A similar question arose in the case of Abdul Wahab Versus The Crown, reported in 7 DLR (FC) 87 and in that case their lordships held as follows: "Where the provisions of Section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure were not complied with but ii appears that the accused is literate and could very well fillow the nature of the proceedings against him, and was also aware of the prosecution case and no miscarriage or failure of justice has been proved in this case, section 53 of the Code of Criminal Procedure would cover it, and for that reason, no interference is called for by this Court." 

 In the instant case, as it appears, the accused-appellant was fully aware of what his son and daughter (PWs. 2 and 3) were stating in the Court on oath in his presence and so also the doctor, his mother-in-law and other witnesses. It is naturally expected that the accused appellant understood the nature of the proceeding and the accusation brought against him and what he was required to do in response thereto. 

 On perusal of the statements made by the accused- appellant under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, we are convinced that he had full knowledge about the nature of accusation and he offered his explanation what he could in the given facts and circumstances of the Case. 

 16. It has been noticed that the PWs.2 and 3 have stated the means of assault to be a loose leg of a table and the PW.10, i-e. the I/O stated it to be a loose, leg of a tool (bench) of pitaraj tree. This type of minor discrepancy' might occur in human testimony. It does not affect merit of the Case. 

 The impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence dated 20.3.2004 passed by the Sessions Judge, Mymensingh, in Sessions Case No. 120 of 2003 arising out of Varakanda Police Station Case No.8 dated I 8.6.2002 corresponding to G.R. No. 294(2) 02 is hereby upheld.
